content:
sophia: Quick flag — after switching our RN sample to the new JS SDK ESM build, iOS device builds fail at runtime. Metro throws on resolving `node:crypto` and Hermes crashes on `crypto.getRandomValues`

sophia: Repro steps: fresh expo init, install @redwood/inference-js@next (ESM), run on device. Error snippet below:

sophia: ```
Error: Unable to resolve module "node:crypto" from 'node_modules/@redwood/inference-js/dist/index.mjs'

ExceptionsManager.js: unhandled JS exception: TypeError: crypto.getRandomValues is not a function
```

mike: Ugh. Pretty classic RN + node builtin mismatch. Two things to try: shim `getRandomValues` and alias `node:crypto` to a rn-friendly polyfill.

mike: In `metro.config.js` we do: ```js
module.exports = {
  resolver: {
    extraNodeModules: { 'node:crypto': require.resolve('react-native-get-random-values') }
  }
}
```

mike: Also ensure you call `import 'react-native-get-random-values'` before any lib that needs crypto.

jordan: Heads up on the TS side: even after shimming, TypeScript complains because `globalThis.crypto` isn't typed in RN projects. I added this in our app declarations: ```ts
declare global {
  interface Crypto {
    getRandomValues(arr: Uint8Array): Uint8Array
  }
  var crypto: Crypto | undefined
}
export {}
```

jordan: That silences the compile errors for me.

sophia: Thanks — that helps. One wrinkle: when using the Edge runtime (Vercel/Cloudflare style) the SDK expects native ESM exports. Metro transforms sometimes wrap CJS -> ESM and change default/named exports; the SDK's `exports` map needs to play nice with RN packager. We're getting `default is not a function` in some cases.

leo: We should publish dual entrypoints: `main` CJS for Node, `module`/`exports` for ESM, and a `react-native` field that points at a rn-specific shim that re-exports and ensures `crypto` import paths are friendly. Also add a tiny wrapper that sets `globalThis.crypto` if missing.

ashley: I opened a PR with a small shim: `rn-shims/crypto-shim.js` that does: ```js
if (typeof globalThis.crypto?.getRandomValues !== 'function') {
  // lightweight fallback using react-native-get-random-values
  require('react-native-get-random-values')
}
module.exports = {}
```

ashley: Then package.json includes: ```json
"react-native": "rn-shims/index.js",
"main": "dist/index.cjs.js",
"module": "dist/index.mjs",
"exports": { ".": { "import": "dist/index.mjs", "require": "dist/index.cjs.js", "react-native": "rn-shims/index.js" } }
```

mike: Nice. One more gotcha — Metro treats `node:` builtin imports specially; aliasing `node:crypto` to a package is necessary, but we should also rewrite internal imports inside the SDK bundle to prefer bare `crypto` or the shim path. Otherwise some bundlers still leave `node:crypto` in transformed code.

jordan: For typings, the SDK should ship `types/react-native.d.ts` that augments `globalThis.crypto` and we should add that path to `package.json` `types` entries so TS finds it in RN projects without manual `declare` hacks.

infra-bot: CI: build/test (rn-sample) triggered by ashley/rn-crypto-shim PR #458 — status: running :gear:

sophia: If CI passes, can we cut a patch release? This is blocking some onboarding flows (new sample app for quickstarts).

leo: Yes, if tests are green I'll bump to 0.9.2 and include a release note describing the `react-native` entry and `rn-shims` behavior. Also add docs snippet for Metro config and `import 'react-native-get-random-values'` ordering.

mike: Suggest adding a tiny E2E Expo CI job to catch hermes vs jsc issues early.

ashley: Agreed. CI added an Expo run on hosted simulators in the PR.

infra-bot: CI: build/test (rn-sample) succeeded — all green :white_check_mark:

ashley: Cut 0.9.2-rc.1 with the shim and RN entrypoint. Please test before I promote to stable.

sophia: Testing now on physical iPhone — will report back in ~10m.

mike: FYI: also tested in a Cloudflare Worker (edge) — ESM bundle works fine when bundler preserves named exports. Might need a note about `default` vs named `createClient` import patterns.

sophia: Confirmed — app boots and no crypto crash on device. TS errors gone after adding the global declaration or using the shipped types. Thanks y'all :tada:

leo: Sweet. Follow-up: file an issue to track `node:` imports in our build pipeline so future ESM bundles avoid leaking them.

jordan: Filed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/789 (track node: imports in RN bundles)

sophia: Closing this thread — great teamwork! :shipit:
